moments.reason: Distance ladder: thumb blots the Moon, Mars is a dot; 250mi→250k→250M.
Supplies rant: 3 min to death, 7s unconscious; 'what a way to die — the toilet broke'.
No free lunches: pay to slow down; aerobrake helps but the last feet are yours.
Sky crane: hover, unreel cables, drop the rover; even its engineers were relieved.
Airbag lander bounced 18 times into Eagle crater — 'hole-in-one'.
Launch windows: committed to 9 months out, a year on the surface, 9 months back.
The Venus flyby: once every 50 years, nightside pass, 'odds of crew surviving probably real good'.
Radiation: 5% excess cancer vs 3% admin limit — 'every single hand would go up'.
Pre-place the propellant plant: want tanks 'freaking full' before crew launches — The Martian tactic.
Nansen's Fram: froze the ship in ice deliberately; 'it's all about the food' — Mars lesson.
Transit ship ≈ ISS-sized; 'what makes human spaceflight interesting is it has humans in it'.
Blue-suit effect: school kids didn't care about the scientist — astronaut suit changed everything.
Moon as stepping stone: 'burst your appendix, home in four days'; the bright star people live in.
Closer: exploration 'brings out the best in us' — only ocean floor and space left.
